scope: Fresh frozen 100-target full Firecrawl v2 API benchmark at context-disposal source9ec9a43. Same dataset, graders, two owners, two page slots per owner, aggregate 5.5GiB browser cap, and persistent one-second monitoring as the preceding complete58/100 source2476425 run. Live epoch and shared host contention can differ, so coverage or latency changes cannot be attributed solely to cleanup. Direct VN egress, four API workers, same deadlines, controls and pacing; no upstream proxies, hosted calls, solvers, expected-text hints, fixture aliases or client retries. Maximum100 API requests and200 browser captures. Unfinished contexts retain their admission slot until actual disposal; capacity loss is observable rather than silently admitting overlapping contexts.

metricDefinitions.normalizedHtml: Successful HTTP/API response with the frozen expected text after markup/script/style/noscript removal and without a detected challenge/page error. Title text is retained; CSS visibility and full-page correctness are not established.
metricDefinitions.normalizedAndMarkdown: Normalized HTML pass and the supplementary frozen literal phrase present in Markdown. A changed heading can miss this phrase even when useful product content is returned.

pacing.limit: Slot reservation precedes fetch. Observed gaps are retained; configuration is not an exact dispatch floor.

fullApiBenchmark.comparisonLimit: Fresh complete 100-target measurement at context-disposal source9ec9a43. The immediately preceding complete58/100 run used the same dataset, graders, two browser owners, page slots, memory caps, and persistent one-second monitoring. These are different live epochs; coverage or latency changes are not independently attributable to cleanup. Memory/PID-limit and OOM events are fatal; socket pressure and PSI qualify timing. No contemporary hosted parity or standalone primary-only score is inferred.

comparisonWithPreviousFullRun.limit: Same frozen workload, graders, limits, workers, owners, and controls, at different live epochs. Coverage and latency changes cannot be attributed solely to the cleanup patch. Socket-pressure and shared-host effects qualify timing.

before.limit: Previous contextClosed receipts reflected fulfilled close commands. One Target acknowledgement was unconfirmed; no retrospective open-context diagnosis is inferred.

contextDisposal.mechanismEvidence: Owned HTTP tests reproduce lost acknowledgements, duplicate commands, and late allocation admission. See the separate development report. A different public run cannot isolate the cleanup effect.
contextDisposal.targetObservation: This run returned Target through WebKit with a close-event receipt. The previous unconfirmed acknowledgement was on Firefox; this is not a paired public Target regression proof. Owned fault-injection tests provide the mechanism evidence.

primary-a.limit: Includes the persistent collector. Shared host/VM contention remains possible; host ancestor cgroups are not visible.

fallback-a.limit: Includes the persistent collector. Shared host/VM contention remains possible; host ancestor cgroups are not visible.

cleanup.inventoryLimit: Only task resources were targeted. Whole-machine inventory can change externally; before/after snapshots do not establish the cause of unrelated changes.

shutdown.limit: An exit0 or termination message alone is not proof of clean worker shutdown.

historicalHostedComparison.limit: Different epoch and provider routing/retry policies. Hosted parity remains unproven.

nextEvidence: Hosted parity remains unproven. Current results must guide the next bounded proxy-free experiment; do not merge partial pilots into this full-run score.

changedTargetInterpretation.lowes: The Firefox alternate remained on the homepage after HTTP200 and returned WORKFLOW_NAVIGATION_MISMATCH. Its document receipt contains subrequest failures including NS_ERROR_NET_RESET. The existing identity guard correctly refused to count the homepage as the requested product. The underlying navigation failure is unresolved.
